disclaimer: KAY9 watchdog reports are automated, probabilistic analyses of public on-chain data. Every signal is a heuristic: it describes what the chain shows, never what anyone intended. Absence of a flag is not a guarantee of safety, presence of a flag is not an accusation of wrongdoing, and no part of this report is financial advice. Nobody pays KAY9 for an audit: access is a refundable lock of KAY9 and nothing a requester does or declares can change a score. Verify the report body against reportHash and the on-chain record before relying on it.

Analysis partial: some data sources were unavailable

notes: A category is scored internally as accumulated risk -- the sum of each signal in that category, weighted by its own confidence, clamped to 0..100 -- and published as trust, 100 minus that accumulation, so a higher published number always means more trustworthy.
Signals are summed in ascending code order so the result does not depend on the order data arrived in.
A category whose data could not be gathered is held at or below a published trust ceiling of 65 and raises INSUFFICIENT_DATA; missing data never raises a trust score.

The published overall trust score is 100 minus the weighted mean of the risk accumulations of the categories this scan actually measured, renormalized to their own combined weight -- a category held at the uncertainty floor does not otherwise pull the headline number toward it -- then held at or below 40 if any scoring signal is high severity and at or below 20 if any is critical. If nothing could be measured, overall sits at the same uncertainty ceiling as any other unmeasured category.

`measuredWeight` (0..1, alongside `confidence`) is the share of the category weight that fed the overall score; a reader should trust a headline number in proportion to it, since a low risk built on a small measured slice is not the same claim as a low risk built on all seven.
Scores are trust, not a quality rating: 100 means nothing risky was observed, 0 means the worst observable state. They are never a recommendation.

Scores from the probabilistic layer -- wallet clustering, Sybil and insider grouping, wash-trading likelihood and creator fingerprinting -- are snapped to the nearest 5 before they are scored, so that independent implementations of those heuristics can agree on a value without coordinating on one. Every signal marked probabilistic in this report was rounded that way; the deterministic core was not.
Categories scored at the uncertainty floor in this run: creator, insider.
methodology.scoring: Each signal contributes points to one risk category internally, weighted by its own confidence; category risk is combined into an overall risk with fixed weights and published as trust, 100 minus that risk. See docs/AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md for the full table.

weights.description: Powers the deployed code grants: minting, pausing, deny-lists, mutable fees, upgradeability, privileged balance movement, and whether source is verified.
Depth of the discovered pools on the quote side, and whether the provider position is locked or burned.
Concentration of circulating supply across the sampled holders, with pools, burn addresses and the token contract itself excluded.
Wallets that share a funding source, and transfers that fund several recipients at once.
The deployer address and the deployment pattern visible in its sampled history.
Round-trip transfer patterns between the same addresses, and whether the token trades at all.
How much of the earliest distribution a small set of addresses captured.

signals.detail: The bytecode contains a function that burns or moves the balance of an account other than the caller. A privileged caller can take or destroy tokens a holder owns.
signals.title: Privileged balance destruction or seizure

signals.detail: No funding source could be resolved for the top holders inside the scanned window, so wallet clustering produced no result.
signals.title: Funding sources for top holders not resolved

signals.detail: Locating a deployment means asking what the chain looked like in the past, which needs an archive node, and enumerating a deployer’s other launches needs an address-indexed transaction history that standard JSON-RPC does not expose. Neither is available to a scan running in a browser against a public endpoint, so no conclusion is drawn about this deployer in either direction.
signals.title: Deployer and deployer history not scanned at this tier

signals.detail: Quote-side depth is above the low-liquidity threshold for this chain.

evidence.label: approximate quote depth in ETH, native pools and priced pools

signals.title: Liquidity present at probed venues

signals.detail: The deployed bytecode dispatches a mint-style function, so new tokens can be created by a caller that passes the access checks. Whether any caller can still do so depends on the owner and role state.
signals.title: Supply can be increased

signals.detail: No Transfer events were seen in the recent window. The token is either dormant or trades entirely outside this window.
signals.title: No transfers in the recent window

signals.detail: owner() did not answer with an address, and no recognised role system was found. That does not mean the privileged functions cannot be called: a custom admin, a role scheme this scanner does not know, or no access control at all would all look like this. Each such function is scored as live.
signals.title: Who controls the privileged functions could not be established

signals.detail: The contract uses role-based access control, so privileges may be held by addresses other than owner(). Renouncing ownership does not necessarily remove them.
signals.title: Role-based access control present

signals.detail: A single non-pool address holds more than half of the circulating supply. Liquidity pools, the token contract and burn addresses were excluded from this calculation.
signals.title: One address holds a majority of the circulating supply

signals.detail: The contract delegates execution to an implementation that an admin can replace. Everything this report says about the current logic can be made untrue by an upgrade.
signals.title: Upgradeable proxy

signals.detail: 100.00% of this token’s priced depth sits in Uniswap v4 positions owned by accounts with no code. Such an owner can remove the liquidity at any time. A lock arranged off chain would not be visible to this check.
signals.title: Liquidity positions are held by ordinary accounts
